To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
multiple preoperative transfusion induces a state of unresponsive that is specific for kidney allografts and is effective in preventing graft loss.
multiple transfusions induce a state of unresponsive that is specific to the donor kidney and is not associated with a generalized suppression of the immune system.
the beneficial effect of transfusions in kidney transplantation is independent of the presence of cytotoxic antibodies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new immunosuppressive drugs and with the use of blood transfusion to induce a state of unresponsive to cadaver donor grafts.
the immunological aspects of kidney transplantation.
the immunosuppression of kidney transplantation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

(1) the beneficial effect of transfusion is not mediated by antibodies; (2) the beneficial effect is probably mediated by an induction of unresponsiveness; and (3) the beneficial effect can be produced by a single transfusion of a large amount of blood, or by a multiple transfusion of a smaller amount of blood.
multiple blood transfusion is an important factor in the induction of unresponsiveness and that this is specific in that there is no alteration in the immune response to other stimuli.
multiple preoperative transfusions of donor-specific blood, as a single treatment, is an effective and safe way of improving kidney graft survival rate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown the beneficial effect of transfusion in the induction of tolerance and the mechanism by which transfusions produce tolerance.
the beneficial effect of transfusion is not due to the presence of antibodies but rather to the presence of a substance that is capable of inducing a state of immunosuppression in the recipient.
multiple transfusion induces a state of unresponsive that does not alter the immunological response to infectious agents and that it is the best way of increasing kidney transplant survival rates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the more transfused the better the transplant outcome.
the immunosuppressant effect is not specific, and the immunosuppressed state can be exploited by opportunistic infections, such as CMV.
multiple transfusions are an easy way to increase kidney transplant survival rates and that this effect does not depend on the development of antibodies.
